top_stories.title: Tenable Identity Exposure SaaS Has CVSS 9.9 Command Injection That Hands Attackers SYSTEM on the Domain Controller
top_stories.summary: A critical command injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-106126) with a CVSS score of 9.9 has been discovered in Tenable Identity Exposure's SaaS platform. The flaw allows attackers to gain SYSTEM-level access on domain controllers, the core infrastructure component managed by identity exposure and Active Directory security tools.

top_stories.title: In the agentic era, standing privilege must go: Key thoughts from the SailPoint Navigate keynote
top_stories.summary: SailPoint used its Navigate 2026 conference keynote in Austin to announce a strategic shift toward real-time access revocation and eliminating standing privileges in the agentic AI era. The company positioned itself as moving beyond traditional identity governance toward dynamic, continuous access control to address risks posed by AI agents operating with persistent permissions.

top_stories.title: How to keep AI agents within their permissions
top_stories.summary: The article addresses the challenge of AI agents operating beyond their assigned permissions despite using valid credentials, a gap in traditional access control models. Token Security outlines approaches for enforcing agent-specific authorization policies while maintaining operational autonomy.

top_stories.title: The AI Velocity Paradox: Why Security Is Decades Behind AI Ambition
top_stories.summary: SailPoint's "Horizons of Identity Security" report identifies a "velocity paradox" where enterprises deploy autonomous AI agents while relying on legacy, human-speed identity security architectures. The report highlights the gap between AI-driven business operations and identity security controls not designed to manage non-human identities at machine speed.

top_stories.title: Citrix Patches Critical NetScaler Flaw That Could Enable RCE in SAML Deployments
top_stories.summary: Citrix has released patches for a critical memory overflow vulnerability (CVE-2026-107406) in NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway that can enable remote code execution or denial-of-service. The flaw specifically affects SAML deployments, making it directly relevant to IAM professionals managing federated identity and authentication infrastructure.

news.title: Credential-Stealing GitHub Actions Workflows Planted in Tens of Thousands of Repositories
news.summary: A credential-theft campaign has compromised two high-profile open-source maintainer accounts to inject malicious GitHub Actions workflows into over 340 repositories. The attacker used the compromised account of pyxel author Takashi Kitao to push malicious workflows to 27 repositories, with the campaign designed to steal credentials from CI/CD pipeline environments.

news.title: PCI SSC calls for human approval of AI agent actions involving cardholder data
news.summary: The PCI Security Standards Council published advisory guidance on AI system security in payment environments, covering governance, deployment, and access controls. The document includes recommendations on human approval requirements for AI agent actions involving cardholder data and addresses defenses against AI-assisted attacks.

news.title: FBI Says China-Linked Hackers Ran Portal Giving Third Parties Access to Stolen Emails
news.summary: The FBI and agencies from six countries reported that hackers linked to Chinese cybersecurity firm Integrity Technology Group stole emails from government, law enforcement, healthcare, and religious organizations in Southeast Asia. The threat actors operated a portal enabling third-party access to stolen email data, with Integrity Technology Group having been sanctioned by both the U.S. and UK governments.

news.title: ‘The gap was not the awareness’: The company phishing trainings you loathe aren’t enough when nearly 1 in 4 security pros say their MFA is optional
news.summary: A survey found that nearly 1 in 4 security professionals report that MFA is optional at their organizations, despite widespread confidence in their company's security posture. The study also found that 44% of respondents experienced a successful AI-driven phishing attack in the past year, highlighting gaps in authentication enforcement.

news.title: U.S. Offers Up to $10 Million for Tips on Zhang Yu, Charged in HAFNIUM Hacks
news.summary: The U.S. State Department is offering up to $10 million for information leading to the identification or location of Zhang Yu, a Chinese national charged in connection with the 2021 HAFNIUM Microsoft Exchange Server attacks. The HAFNIUM attacks exploited zero-day vulnerabilities in Microsoft Exchange Server to gain unauthorized access to thousands of organizations' email systems and networks.

news.title: ID Dataweb Named "Overall ID Management Solution of the Year" in the 2026 CyberSecurity Breakthrough Awards Program
news.summary: ID Dataweb was named "Overall ID Management Solution of the Year" in the 2026 CyberSecurity Breakthrough Awards Program. The award recognizes the company's approach to identity threat detection and risk mitigation for enterprises.

news.title: Anugal Announces U.S. SAP IDM Readiness Campaign Ahead of 2027 Maintenance Deadline
news.summary: Anugal, a product of Business Core Solutions, has launched a U.S. campaign to help enterprises prepare for the SAP Identity Management (SAP IDM) end-of-maintenance deadline in 2027. The campaign focuses on uncovering hidden SAP IDM dependencies and supporting organizations in migrating or modernizing their identity governance infrastructure before support ends.

news.title: The people who know passkeys best are still typing passwords
news.summary: A Yubico and Okta survey of 1,890 technology and security professionals across nine countries found that 43% still primarily use usernames and passwords for work accounts, despite 87% reporting familiarity with passkeys. The findings highlight a gap between passkey awareness and adoption among the professionals most expected to lead authentication modernization.

news.title: SonicWall Patches CVSS 10.0 Pre-Authentication SSRF Flaw in SMA1000 Appliances
news.summary: SonicWall has released hotfixes addressing four vulnerabilities in its SMA1000 appliances, including a CVSS 10.0 pre-authentication SSRF flaw. The critical flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to send requests through the appliance to reach internal network functions, affecting remote access gateway infrastructure.

news.title: FBI Warns FortiBleed Remains Active After Amassing 86,644 Fortinet Device Credentials
news.summary: The FBI and USSS issued a warning that the FortiBleed credential harvesting campaign remains active, having collected 86,644 credentials from internet-facing Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways. The campaign exploits reused or leaked credentials and legacy SHA-256 password storage vulnerabilities in Fortinet devices.

news.title: Browser-in-browser attacks use fake Meta Muse Ad lure to steal credentials
news.summary: A browser-in-the-browser (BitB) phishing attack campaign is using fake Meta Muse advertisements to steal user credentials. The attack creates convincing fake browser windows within the real browser to deceive users into entering their login information on fraudulent pages.

news.title: ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude imitated in fake ads that steal credentials and MFA codes
news.summary: Cybercriminals are running fake ads impersonating AI platforms ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude to steal credentials and MFA codes from victims. The campaign specifically targets advertiser accounts that have pre-loaded credit cards and funds, using credential theft and MFA bypass techniques.

news.title: Half of Cybersecurity Pros Still Rely on Passwords Despite Security Concerns
news.summary: A Yubico survey found that half of cybersecurity professionals still rely on passwords as a primary authentication method despite awareness of their security risks. The study highlights a gap between enterprise knowledge of more secure authentication methods and actual adoption of those methods.

news.title: High Awareness, Low Adoption: New Survey Reveals Nearly Half of Security Professionals Still Rely on Passwords
news.summary: A joint survey by Yubico and Okta found that nearly half of security professionals still rely on passwords despite widespread awareness of stronger authentication alternatives. The global study highlights an adoption gap in enterprise security regarding modern identity controls and passwordless authentication methods.

news.title: Stop Hoping for Secure AI and Start Building It: RSA Agent ID Closes the Agentic Identity Gap for Highly Regulated Industries
news.summary: RSA has launched Agent ID, a solution designed to address identity and authentication challenges for AI agents operating in regulated industries such as finance and government. The product enables organizations to discover, register, and verify the authority of AI agents, positioning it within the emerging agentic identity management space.

news.title: SailPoint’s 40x Gap — Enterprise AI Agent Adoption Has Outrun Identity Security by a Factor of 40
news.summary: SailPoint's Navigate 2026 conference in Austin revealed that enterprise AI agent adoption has outpaced identity security measures by a factor of 40. The data presented highlights a significant gap between AI agent deployment rates and the identity security controls organizations have in place to manage them.

news.title: Improving SPIRE security and resiliency with AWS managed services
news.summary: The article covers improving SPIRE (SPIFFE Runtime Environment) security and resiliency using AWS managed services for workload identity in cloud environments. SPIRE is an open-source implementation of the SPIFFE standard for machine-to-machine identity and authentication, replacing traditional static credentials like API keys and shared secrets.

news.title: Fake ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude Ad Portals Capture Credentials and MFA Codes
news.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a human-operated phishing platform that impersonates advertising portals for major AI chatbots including ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude to steal credentials and MFA codes. The platform targets users by mimicking legitimate AI product advertisements to capture authentication data including multi-factor authentication codes.

news.title: Kiteworks & Citrix Incidents Show Challenges of Zero-Day Response
news.summary: Kiteworks and Citrix both faced zero-day vulnerability incidents, with Kiteworks instructing customers to power down its data-protection platform during a nine-hour window as part of its response. Citrix took a different approach, remaining silent on reported attacks until releasing a patch, highlighting divergent vendor disclosure practices around zero-day response.

news.title: SWIFT Banking & Government Middleware Enables RCE
news.summary: A vulnerability in SWIFT banking and government middleware has been identified that enables remote code execution (RCE). The flaw can be exploited to bypass hardware-based MFA in high-security environments, with patching recommended as the immediate mitigation.

news.title: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
news.summary: Microsoft released a record-breaking patch batch addressing at least 974 security vulnerabilities across Windows operating systems and other software. The company attributed the increased vulnerability discovery rate in part to AI-assisted research, while security experts noted organizations are struggling to prioritize and deploy the high volume of monthly fixes.

news.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
news.summary: A dark web service is selling digital scans of over 153 million drivers licenses from the US and Canada, apparently sourced from a Louisiana-based identity verification company. The FBI's New Orleans field office has launched an official inquiry into the breach, which involves compromised identity verification infrastructure.
